note: THE MARINE FAULT TAXONOMY. A signature is a physical *reading* an instrument can produce. A class is a *cause* — the thing a surveyor would write on the report. The instrument produces signatures; the surveyor produces causes. This file keeps the two apart, because conflating them is how an instrument starts claiming to know things it cannot know.
_thePoint: Three of the moisture classes below — condensation, active ingress, historic salt — produce the *same reading*. No single measurement separates them. That is not a weakness of this design; it is the reason the product is a deployment with a time series rather than a handheld meter, and the reason the report says 'a moisture anomaly of an undetermined cause' instead of guessing. The taxonomy's value is in the parts that name what cannot be determined as precisely as the parts that can.
_onNotObservable: A class with `observable: not_observable` is not a defect in the taxonomy. It is a permanent limit of any instrument that cannot see, and stating it is worth more than a number that pretends otherwise. Corrosion at dissimilar metals needs eyes. No swarm will ever clear that, and a product that promises to will be caught out on the first hull.
_onSignatures: A class lists every reading that can indicate it. Most list one. `blocked_drainage` lists two, because a blocked drain presents as an obstructed passage *or* as an obstruction on the map, depending on where you look at it. The oracle's per-instance `signature` picks the reading for that instance; the taxonomy lists the possibilities.

signatures.reading: Relative humidity above the agent's own running baseline, sustained across three consecutive readings.
signatures.resolutionRequires: A time series, and a wash cycle. An active leak rises after the deck is washed; condensation tracks the skin temperature and the diurnal cycle; historic salt sits in equilibrium with the boat's own ambient. A single reading cannot separate them, and a report that says it can is lying.
signatures.note: Five causes, one reading. The single most important row in this file.

signatures.reading: Surface temperature deviating from a baseline the agent estimated for itself, in two or more adjacent bearings.
signatures.resolutionRequires: A load correlation, or a second instrument. A hot spot is a symptom; the cause is what is failing under it.
signatures.note: Relative, not absolute. A fixed threshold cannot cancel an unknown emissivity offset, and the naive absolute detector is kept in the codebase as the control so the difference can be measured rather than asserted.

signatures.reading: A passage obstructed — an air path, a drain, or the bore of a conduit.
signatures.instrument: Air/VOC proxy at a registered port; forward range finder inside a conduit
signatures.resolutionRequires: Eyes, and the run of the system. The instrument says a passage is obstructed; which passage, and what is blocking it, comes from the manifold the reading was taken on and from a person.
signatures.note: One reading, three causes, three different manifolds. The manifold is what disambiguates it, and the manifold is a fact about the vessel, not about the sensor.

signatures.reading: A mapped, non-blocking obstruction on the sole or a surface.
signatures.resolutionRequires: Eyes. A geometric obstruction has no cause attached to it.
signatures.note: Known to over-fire. Without a camera this reports soft furnishings and stowed gear as hazards, and that over-fire is the measured cost of deferring RGB, not a defect to be hidden.

signatures.reading: A surface discontinuity in the occupancy map.
signatures.resolutionRequires: Ultrasonic thickness measurement or percussion, and then eyes.
signatures.note: Known-pessimistic. A hairline crack in a surface is below what a depth camera resolves.

classes.name: Condensation in a void
classes.secondObservable: Temperature gradient against the skin; the diurnal cycle
classes.corroborationMethod: RH correlated with skin temperature over at least one diurnal cycle
classes.remedy: Ventilate the void, dry it, and re-read. If it returns with the dew point, the void is doing this on its own and the fix is airflow and insulation, not a leak repair.
classes.note: The most common void fault and the one nobody reports, because it needs somebody to have been in there.

classes.name: Active water ingress
classes.secondObservable: Response to a wash cycle; a point source
classes.corroborationMethod: RH rises after the deck is washed, and decays when the source is stopped
classes.remedy: Find the source and reseal it. Fix the penetration, not the symptom.
classes.note: A leak is worth money because it is progressive. A survey that says 'no leak' on a boat nobody could get into is not a clearance, it is an absence of evidence.

classes.name: Historic salt in the core — hygroscopic equilibrium
classes.corroborationMethod: Sampling only. The instrument can say the void is in equilibrium with ambient; it cannot say why.
classes.remedy: Nothing urgent. This is a record item — it tells the next owner the core has salt in it.
classes.note: The honest answer is 'consistent with hygroscopic salt, not provable without a sample'. Saying more than that would be the first lie the product tells.

classes.name: Deck penetration leak — cleat, stanchion, winch, mast step
classes.corroborationMethod: Local RH at the fixing, with the fixing identified in the map
classes.remedy: Re-bed the fixing and reseal. The chandlery's work: a new gasket, a new seal, a re-bedded deck fitting.
classes.note: A point source with a known cause. The most actionable thing this instrument finds, and the easiest for an owner to act on.

classes.name: Bilge high or bilge pump fault
classes.corroborationMethod: Depth reading that persists with the pump confirmed running
classes.remedy: Clear the strainer, check the pump, then check the automatic float switch.
classes.note: High severity, easy to miss, and it is the one that stops the boat.

classes.name: Exhaust leak or water ingress to the engine
classes.secondObservable: Sound; a wet exhaust manifold seen from the inlet
classes.corroborationMethod: Thermal alone does not name it. A leak past the gasket is the yard's call.
classes.remedy: Replace the gasket. Check the water injection and the exhaust elbow for the same cause.
classes.note: Thermal is the giveaway because the exhaust runs hot and a leak runs colder than the surrounding metal.

classes.name: Overheating bearing
classes.secondObservable: Vibration; lubricant temperature; inspection after shutdown
classes.corroborationMethod: Temperature rise correlated with load, plus vibration at the same bearing
classes.remedy: Find out why it is running hot before it seizes. This is a stop-the-boat finding if it is confirmed.
classes.note: The highest-consequence fault in the engine room and the one a sound survey catches late.

classes.name: Hot electrical connection
classes.secondObservable: Infrared survey; torque check on the connection
classes.corroborationMethod: Thermal rise at a connection that correlates with load
classes.remedy: Clean and re-torque. This is a fire risk and it is treated as one.
classes.note: Cheap to fix, expensive to ignore. A good example of a thermal finding with a definite remedy.

classes.name: Blocked ventilation or extraction
classes.secondObservable: Airflow; stale air standing against the engine bay outlet
classes.corroborationMethod: The air proxy stays high at the port while the extractor is running
classes.remedy: Clear the inlet, clean the fan, check the duct. Then re-measure the draw.
classes.note: Poor extraction raises the temperature of everything in the engine bay, which makes every other thermal finding harder to read.

classes.name: Blocked drainage
classes.corroborationMethod: Obstruction in the map, plus water that does not drain
classes.remedy: Clear the scuppers and the drains. Low cost, high nuisance value — a deck that holds water is a deck that finds its way into the saloon.
classes.note: The one class that presents two ways: an obstructed passage, or an obstruction on the map, depending on where you look. Neither reading distinguishes it from a stowed object.

classes.name: Debris in the bilge
classes.secondObservable: Bilge-water depth and what is floating in it
classes.corroborationMethod: Obstruction in the map, plus standing water
classes.remedy: Lift it out, find out what it came from, and check the thing it came from.
classes.note: Mostly harmless on its own. It matters because it is evidence of something that is not.

classes.name: Obstruction in a fuel line
classes.secondObservable: None available from inside the bore
classes.corroborationMethod: None from this manifold. The crawler can say the bore is obstructed; what it is, takes the line apart.
classes.remedy: Isolate, blow through, and replace the section. Not a job to guess at.
classes.note: The one place where the swarm is inside something a person cannot comfortably be. A 60 mm fuel line is a good place to put a robot and a bad place to put a person.

classes.name: Weld defect or porosity
classes.remedy: Grind out and re-weld, or a doubler plate, per the yard.
classes.note: A geometric proxy for something ultrasonic. The proxy is known-pessimistic and is reported as its own series.

classes.name: Hull stress crack
classes.secondObservable: Ultrasonic thickness mapping along the run of the plating
classes.remedy: Stop the boat and get the class society involved. This one is not a chandlery job.
classes.note: The most serious cause behind the structural-crack reading, and the least distinguishable from a weld defect by any of the instruments we have.

classes.name: Machinery vibration or misalignment
classes.secondObservable: An accelerometer, and the load correlation that goes with it
classes.corroborationMethod: Load correlation against the machine's own duty cycle
classes.remedy: Align it. Couplings and bearings, and a lot of engine room time.
classes.note: A DETECTOR GAP, NOT A SENSOR GAP. The crawler carries an accelerometer for its own state; nothing interprets it as machinery vibration yet. That is a week of work, not a platform, and it is written here so it is not forgotten.

classes.name: Corrosion at dissimilar metals or fittings
classes.secondObservable: None from this instrument. Eyes, and a borescope.
classes.corroborationMethod: Requires a pair of eyes. There is no substitute and there is not going to be one.
classes.remedy: Replace the fitting, isolate the two metals, and coat it.
classes.note: PERMANENTLY OUT OF REACH. This class is in the taxonomy precisely so the product's boundary is written down instead of discovered by a customer.

classes.name: Unrecorded modification or penetration
classes.corroborationMethod: Compare the configuration to the surveyor's record. This is a check, not a measurement.
classes.remedy: Record it. That is the whole remedy — the risk of an unrecorded penetration is that it is unknown, not that it exists.
classes.note: Worth real money and it is not a sensor problem. It is a records problem, and the product's report is a records document.
